chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me: 'Verily, there is a virtue with you (or: close to you) which has not been given to anyone else. And I do not think you know its true essence, nor do you adhere to it, nor do you commit to performing it. And verily, it has a specific group of people who have been named for it, and it was bestowed upon them without any effort or power from themselves, except by the will of Allah, and it is a happiness that Allah gifted them with, a mercy, compassion, and precedence.'
I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what is this that you have described to us but did not name?'

He said: 'The Ziyarah (visitation) of my grandfather, Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him). Verily, he is a stranger in a land of strangeness. Those who visit him weep for him, and those who do not visit him grieve for him, and those who do not see him burn with anguish for him, and those who look at the grave of his son at his feet in a barren land, have mercy on him. He had no close intimate friend nor any relative.'

Then they denied his right, and the people of apostasy conspired against him until they killed him, neglected him, and exposed him to beasts. They prevented him from drinking the water of the Euphrates, which even dogs drink. And they neglected the right of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his will concerning him and his family.

So he remained abandoned in his grave, struck down among his kin and his Shia, between layers of dust. His closeness was made lonely in solitude, and far from his grandfather and the house, which is not visited except by those whose hearts Allah tested for faith and whom He made to know our rights.

I said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I used to go to him until I was afflicted with the ruler and guarding their wealth, and I was well-known among them. So I left going to him for precaution (Taqiyyah), although I know the good in going to him.'
He said: 'Do you know the merit of those who go to him, and what he has with us of abundant good?' I said: 'No.'
He said: 'As for the merit, the angels of the heavens boast about it. And as for what he has with us, it is that we seek mercy for him every morning and evening.'
And my father (peace be upon him) narrated to me that his place has not been empty since he was killed, from one praying blessings upon him from among the angels, or the Jinn, or mankind, or beasts.
And there is nothing that does not envy his visitor, touch him, and hope for good by looking at him for having looked at his grave (peace be upon him).
Then he said: 'It has reached me that a group comes to him from the suburbs of Kufah, and people from elsewhere, and women who lament for him, and that is in the middle of Sha'ban.'
Among them are a reciter who recites, a narrator who tells stories, a lamentor who laments, and a speaker who recites elegies.
I said: 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you, I have witnessed some of what you describe.'

He said: 'Praise be to Allah who made among the people those who come to us, praise us, and eulogize us. And He made our enemy those who slander them from among our kin, and others who incite them and condemn what they do.'

key_terms.زِيَارَةُ جَدِّيَ الْحُسَيْنِ: The visitation of my grandfather Al-Husayn
key_terms.يُبَاهِيهِ مَلَائِكَةُ السَّمَاءِ: The angels of the heavens boast about it

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual merits and rewards of visiting Imam Al-Husayn's grave according to Imam Al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) elevates Ziyarat al-Husayn as a distinct, divinely bestowed virtue, emphasizing the cosmic significance where angels boast of visitors and the Imam himself intercedes for them. The narration contextualizes the grave as a site of profound solitude and grief, contrasting the betrayal of the 'people of apostasy' with the enduring devotion of the faithful, particularly highlighting the communal mourning rituals observed in mid-Sha'ban.
